ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit

and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  March 12, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 12, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary/ Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/ Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing
  Authority Members/Finance Authority Members/Parking
  Authority Members/ Joint Powers Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint
  Powers Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:
  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/ Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/ Joint Powers Authority on any item on
  the Agendas.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated March 8, 2024,
  in the amount of $6,995,601.75, and dated February 29, 2024, in the amount of
  $3,326,118.77 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing
  Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands
  are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that the Minutes for the City Council Meeting held on December 12, 2023, be
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
 March 12, 2024

142  MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENTS NOS. 24-149 APPROVED – U.S. NATIONAL
  CORP DBA JIMENEZ PAINTING COMPANY, SKY JTC CORPORATION, AND
  CHPC INC. Staff report dated March 12, 2024, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members approve three (3)-year Master Services Agreements to
  provide repainting and refinishing services, per solicitation number RFQu-009.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby approve Master Services Agreements Nos. 24-149 in a
  combined contract amount not to exceed $500,000 with the following consultants:
  A) U.S. National Corp dba Jimenez Painting Company;
  B) SKY JTC Corporation; and
  C) CHPC Inc.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

171  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – AQUA-FLO SUPPLY. Staff report dated March 12,
  2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members authorize
  payment of two (2) invoices submitted by Aqua-Flo Supply for materials, such as industrial
  valves, water main metal repair clamps, and irrigation sprinklers needed by the Parks
  Division.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the total amount of $3,510.17. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  TERMINATION OF AGREEMENT NO. 19-002 APPROVED – DICTATION
  SALES AND SERVICE, INC. DBA EQUATURE; SUCCESSOR AGREEMENT NO.
  24-150 APPROVED – DICTATION SALES AND SERVICE, INC DBA EQUATURE.
  Staff report dated March 12, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members approve a five (5)-year successor agreement with Dictation Sales and
  Service, Inc. dba Equature to provide upgraded hardware and software and ongoing
  licenses, services, and maintenance for the digital recording system.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve termination of Agreement No. 19-002 with
  Dictation Sales and Service, Inc. dba Equature to allow for successor agreement; and 2)
  Approve five (5)-year successor Agreement No. 24-150 in a total amount not to exceed
  $170,980. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – AMERICAN BIKE PATROL SERVICES (ABPS).
  Staff report dated March 12, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and
  Council Members authorize payment of a partial invoice submitted by American Bike Patrol
  Services (ABPS) for bicycle parts and services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $697.87. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and

  (BVP) FUNDS ACCEPTED. Staff report dated March 12, 2024, was presented

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-151 APPROVED – JCI
  JONES CHEMICALS, INC. Staff report dated March 12, 2024, was presented
  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve a one

131.8  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-152 APPROVED –

  recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and approve a two
  (2)-year agreement (with the option to extend up to two (2) years, in one (1)-year

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-152 in a total
  amount not to exceed $285,974 ($142,987 per year), as funding is available. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

173  ORDINANCE NO. 24-05 ADOPTED - SALARY ORDINANCE FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2023-2024. Staff report dated March 12, 2024, was presented recommending that the
  Mayor and Council Members adopt Ordinance No. 24-05, establishing pay range
  assignment and conditions of employment for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that Ordinance No. 24-05 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT FOR THE VARIOUS OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND
  POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE OF THE CITY FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024;
  INCLUDING THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR (ITC) GRANT
  FUNDED TRANSITIONAL APPOINTMENTS AND REPEALING ALL
  PREVIOUS ORDINANCES OF THE CITY IN CONFLICT OR AT VARIANCE
  THEREWITH; THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOW:

  which was introduced at the meeting held on February 27, 2024, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  3
 March 12, 2024

114  APPOINTMENT TO THE HOUSING ADVISORY BOARD RATIFIED – AT
  LARGE. Mayor Butts made an appointment to the Housing Advisory Board for the term
  ending March 2026 to Maude E. Jones. The appointment was carried and ratified by the
  following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  Mae Wood, a 35-year resident, spoke about an incident she witnessed on Market Street a
  couple of weeks ago. She stated that she saw a young lady running past her in high heels, trying
  to avoid getting a parking ticket. Mae also stated that she couldn’t believe how fast  the
  young lady was running, but parking enforcement informed her that it was too late  since
  the ticket had already been written. She added that the young lady begged parking
  enforcement to give her another chance, but nothing could be done about the ticket. Mae
  explained that the young lady took the ticket and sat in her car with her head on her
  steering wheel. After witnessing this, Mae also explained that she stood there until the  young
  lady composed herself.

  Additionally, she discussed the conversation with the young lady regarding the ticket and
  gave her ten dollars to offer assistance. Mae also discussed how apologetic she was to the
  young lady and the traffic officers, explaining that there was nothing else they could do.
  Furthermore, she said the young lady couldn’t afford the ticket because she had no money.
  Finally, she mentioned her reasoning for bringing this incident to the Council.

114  APPOINTMENT TO THE HOUSING ADVISORY BOARD RESCINDED. Mayor
  Butts recommended that the previous vote be rescinded because the appointee's name wasn’t
  mentioned at the beginning of the appointment.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby rescind the previous vote of the appointment to the Housing Advisory
  Board. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

114  APPOINTMENT TO THE HOUSING ADVISORY BOARD RATIFIED – AT
  LARGE. Mayor Butts appointed Maude E. Jones to the Housing Advisory Board for the
  term ending March 2026. The appointment was carried and ratified by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  PUBLIC REMARKS CONTINUED. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business
  not elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) thanked the Mayor and Council Members for allowing him to
  speak at the City Council Meeting. The father expressed his gratitude for all the events
  during his time in Inglewood and for the well-rounded education his children received at
  Wilder's Academy. Finally, he mentioned that he would always oppose what the
  governor and others were doing to children without parental consent.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) thanked the Council for allowing Inglewood residents to
  speak. She stated that she had lived in Inglewood for 13 years and had seen good and bad
  changes. She also stated that she wanted to bring to the Council's attention the change in
  tenants with dogs. She mentioned that in front of her apartment complex on Queen Street,
  people walk their dogs without cleaning up behind them. The speaker also mentioned that
  she was unsure of how to handle this or who to complain to. She recommended more
  patrolling but did not have the answer and felt it should be addressed. Finally, she noted
  how unsanitary it was to defile the walking areas with animal feces.
